set.layering_notes: Riverside County's Housing and Workforce Solutions (HWS) department runs the Urban County HUD programs, PLHA, HHAP, Homekey+ sponsorships and project loans, while the Housing Authority of the County of Riverside (HACR, same Board sitting as Commissioners) supplies project-based vouchers, housing successor funds and land; rivcohws.org and harivco.org block automated access, so records were built from Board of Supervisors files on riversidecountyca.iqm2.com and media.rivcocob.org, RUHS Behavioral Health, the Assessor and the County Housing Element. Unlike several Bay Area counties, Riverside chose tenant-based subsidies and operating support over project-based commitments and zero capital, so BHSA is not a construction source here; developers of PSH should seek RUHS-BH operating subsidy or master lease vendor agreements for behavioral health units and pair them with HACR PBVs. Source is the DHCS Integrated Plan submission (RUHS media 5601); executive brief at ruhealth.org/media/5971; Board adoption file Detail_LegiFile.aspx?ID=30512. Audit 2026-11-08: classified as grant because the BHSA Housing Interventions plan funds rental subsidies (6,015 people a year) and operating subsidies (725 people) for housing; the plan answers No to capital development, so it is a rental and operating subsidy grant source, not a capital source.

reason: Integrated Plan confirms BHSA housing funds go to rental and operating subsidies with no capital, so funding_type is grant per the BHSA rule; figures match the plan.

set.typical_award_size: Revolving predevelopment loan fund for affordable housing in the Coachella Valley, managed by Lift to Rise. The County contributed $2,000,000 of District 4 ARPA funds on May 24, 2022, and the Board added $1,500,000 for Lift to Rise to advance affordable housing throughout Riverside County in the FY 2026-27 budget adjustments approved June 9, 2026 (the release does not say the $1.5M goes to the Catalyst Fund itself). Lift to Rise's action plan targets 10,000 affordable homes in ten years with more than 50 regional partners.
set.layering_notes: Riverside County's Housing and Workforce Solutions (HWS) department runs the Urban County HUD programs, PLHA, HHAP, Homekey+ sponsorships and project loans, while the Housing Authority of the County of Riverside (HACR, same Board sitting as Commissioners) supplies project-based vouchers, housing successor funds and land; rivcohws.org and harivco.org block automated access, so records were built from Board of Supervisors files on riversidecountyca.iqm2.com and media.rivcocob.org, RUHS Behavioral Health, the Assessor and the County Housing Element. The Catalyst Fund is the only revolving predevelopment source in the eastern county and is often the first money into Coachella and Indio tax credit deals before County PLHA, HOME and HACR PBVs; the fund itself and CVAG's housing programs belong in Pass 4 and Pass 3. Source is the County news release on the 2022 contribution (rivco.gov/node/589 now redirects to the news URL); FY 2026-27 budget action at rivco.gov/node/7036.

reason: Old node URL redirects to the County news release, which confirms the $2M ARPA contribution and predevelopment loan purpose; the FY 2026-27 release confirms the $1.5M Lift to Rise add but not that it is earmarked to the fund.
